abstract:
This trail follows the route from the thermodynamics of horizons to Einstein's equations. [[t]] Black-hole temperature and entropy alone cannot single out Einstein's theory, because a whole family of theories shares the same black holes. [[c:synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-field-equations]]

Jacobson's argument closes the gap by applying the heat law $\delta Q = T\,\delta S$ to every small horizon that matter crosses. [[c:synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995]] Under the series' local-horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), the store proves Einstein's equations along that route, with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]]

The remaining steps take the premise apart: its temperature clauses are one joint thermal condition, and its third clause adds nothing beyond them. [[c:synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity]]
introduction: The walk first says why black holes alone are not enough, then sets out the two imported tools, then proves the equations, and ends by examining what the premise it rests on actually contains. [[t]]
i:einstein: Each step either supplies an ingredient of the thermodynamic route to Einstein's equations or tests the premise that route needs. [[t]]
t:^>synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix:
We start from what the series already has: black holes with a temperature, a count of modes and an entropy. [[t]]

Every Lagrangian \[ \frac{R}{16\pi G} + f(\mathrm{Ric}) \] with $f$ at least quadratic in the Ricci tensor shares the Schwarzschild field, its temperature and, assuming Wald entropy, its entropy $A/4G$. [[c:synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-field-equations]] So these inputs cannot pick out Einstein's equations; what would separate the theories is entropy on local horizons crossed by matter. [[c:synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-field-equations]]
t:synthesis.black-hole-data-do-not-fix-f:
The first tool is geometry. [[t]]

A bundle of light rays focuses as it travels: its expansion $\theta$ obeys \[ (k \cdot D)\theta = -\theta^{2}/2 - \sigma^{2} + \omega^{2} - \Ric^{\circ}(k,k) \] with $\sigma$ the shear and $\omega$ the twist. [[c:synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence]] Matter and field strength along the rays pull them together, so the area of the bundle shrinks. [[c:synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-congruence]]
t:synthesis.imported-raychaudhuri-null-c:
The second tool is thermodynamics. [[t]]

If every local Rindler horizon has the Unruh temperature, an entropy $\eta$ per unit area, and obeys $\delta Q = T\,\delta S$ for the matter's boost-energy flux, then the gravitational field obeys \[ \mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -(2\pi/\eta)\,T(a) \] with $\Lambda$ undetermined. [[c:synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995]] This is Jacobson's 1995 result, written in the store's sign. [[c:synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1995]]
t:synthesis.imported-jacobson-clausius-1:
The series' local-horizon premise (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) supplies the temperature and the entropy, and this step carries the argument through inside the store. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]]

Every further hypothesis is stated: Clausius with $\delta S = \eta\,\delta A$, a thin patch with vanishing expansion and shear, a conserved $T_{ab}$, a $C^{3}$ derived metric, four dimensions. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]] Then \[ \mathcal{R}(a) + 8\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,T(a) = (\Lambda + 4\pi G_{\mathrm{cl}}\,\tau)\,a \] with $\Lambda$ an integration constant and $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 1/(4\eta)$. [[c:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-loc-and-clausius]]
t:synthesis.einstein-equations-from-c-lo:
The derivation is conditional, so the rest of the walk asks what the premise contains. [[t]]

Its temperature clauses are one condition: joint KMS for the local boost at rapidity period $2\pi$, a new premise stronger than the local form of (R). [[c:synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity]] Derived is only the geometric half, that this period is where the local boost's Euclidean section is regular, giving \[ T = a/2\pi \] up to a relative correction of order $\rho^{2}$. [[c:synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-local-regularity]]
t:synthesis.local-boost-temperature-is-l:
Next the entropy clause. [[t]]

If the entropy density of a small patch depends only on its flat tangent data, not on the field strength or matter at the point, the Lorentz group forces one universal constant $\eta$. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density]] Calibrated on the Schwarzschild family under (P), (R) and Hawking's hypothesis, \[ \eta = \tfrac14 \] with no mode count. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density]] That independence from curvature excludes the Wald-type entropies of the rival theories met at the start. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvature-independent-density]]
t:synthesis.c-loc-entropy-clause-curvatu:
Putting modes on every horizon raises a bookkeeping question, because the cutoff premises place a black hole's modes at a locus inside its horizon. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-of-the-count]]

If the two placements are independent and the hole's entropy is the total over all its modes, Jacobson's constant becomes $G_{\mathrm{cl}} = 2G$ at the area-law calibration. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-of-the-count]] If they are identified, they inherit the literal Kerr count's conflict with $A_{+}/4$, which counts against the cutoff placement on spinning holes, not against (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$). [[c:synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-of-the-count]]
t:synthesis.c-loc-is-a-second-placement-:
The last step looks at the third clause as first written, that the modes' modular flow acts geometrically on nested sub-patches. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch]]

A boost acting by phases is almost periodic, so it maps no closed subspace properly into itself and cannot push a smaller patch into a larger one. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch]] The clause is consistent only as the boost dynamics on the whole patch, where for a faithful state it restates the temperature clause. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-modular-clause-moves-no-nested-patch]]
conclusion:
The thread runs from black holes that cannot choose a theory of gravity, through the focusing of light and the heat law on small horizons, to Einstein's equations proved under one premise. [[t]]

That premise, (C$_{\mathrm{loc}}$), has two parts: an entropy $\int\eta\,dA$ per cut with $\eta$ independent of the field strength and matter, and modes on every local horizon that are jointly KMS for the local boost before matter crosses. [[c:synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise]] Deriving either part from the series' own structure is still open. [[t]]
